about: Customer-safe Server to Relativity aiR compatibility catalog. Every entry stands on Relativity's public documentation.

entries.title: Direct SQL access through IDBContext
entries.replacement: Object Manager API and the other Kepler services
entries.customer_wording: Relativity aiR still documents IDBContext, but direct SQL from app code isn't a long-term path in the cloud. Relativity's scripts guidance notes that data stored in SQL may be moved to different storage in the future, and transactions opened inside the SQL text (BEGIN TRAN) aren't supported. For anything you're porting or building new, use Object Manager and the other Relativity APIs instead of GetDBContext.

docs.title: Advanced code sample for database interactions

entries.title: Direct SQL access to Processing datastores (INV databases)
entries.replacement: Processing API (v2)
entries.customer_wording: Direct SQL access to the Processing datastores (the INV databases) was removed from aiR on March 18, 2026, per the Developer Changelog. If your code or scripts query those databases, that workflow needs to move to the Processing API.

entries.title: Direct SQL access to the EDDSArchiving database
entries.replacement: ARM REST API V3
entries.customer_wording: Per the Developer Changelog, direct SQL access to the EDDSArchiving database is removed in aiR as of October 1, 2026. Integrations that read ARM job state from that database need to move to the ARM REST API V3.

entries.title: Custom SQL triggers in Relativity databases
entries.replacement: Event handlers, or polling through Object Manager
entries.customer_wording: The Developer Changelog (May 1, 2026) says custom SQL triggers in Relativity databases should no longer be used in aiR. If your app installs triggers to react to data changes, move that logic into event handlers, or poll for changes through Object Manager.

entries.title: Reading logs from EDDSLogging or local log files
entries.replacement: External Logging (preferred) or IAPILog
entries.customer_wording: The aiR docs don't cover reading Relativity's log tables or local log folders the way Server does. The documented approach for apps is External Logging, where your app sends its own logs (Serilog, ILogger, and so on) to a logging service you control, configured through your app's instance settings (LoggingLevel, LoggingEndpoint, LoggingToken). Plan on wiring that up as part of the move.

entries.title: Direct fileshare and UNC path access
entries.replacement: Relativity Transfer SDK, Import Service API, Export Service API
entries.customer_wording: aiR doesn't give apps open access to the fileshare. Since June 2023 agents no longer connect to every fileshare on startup, and since September 2024 staging boundaries block reading or writing outside the defined staging area, with the FTA, Temp, Export, and dtSearch folders removed. Move file work off UNC paths and onto the Relativity Transfer SDK and the Import and Export Service APIs.

entries.title: Server SDK packages (Relativity.Server.* from Artifactory)
entries.replacement: Matching Relativity.* packages on nuget.org, normal aiR packaging
entries.customer_wording: aiR apps build against the Relativity packages on nuget.org, not the Relativity.Server.* packages from the Server feeds, and Server RAP Builder doesn't build aiR packages. The SDK comparison page lists the matching aiR package for each Server one, and Relativity's guidance is to keep separate Server and aiR branches. For a lot of apps this ends up being mostly a package swap and a rebuild.

entries.title: RSAPI (Relativity Services API)
entries.replacement: Object Manager API and the per-domain Kepler services (see RSAPI migration matrix)
entries.customer_wording: RSAPI is gone in aiR. It stopped working on October 23, 2021, and it was also removed from Server 2023. Code that uses kCura.Relativity.Client needs to move to Object Manager and the other Kepler services, and the RSAPI migration matrix maps each feature to its replacement.

entries.title: Unversioned Audit API
entries.replacement: Versioned Audit API (REST and .NET)
entries.customer_wording: The unversioned Audit API was deprecated in aiR in June 2023, so code that references Relativity.Audit.Services.Unversioned.Interfaces or calls the non-versioned URL needs to move to the versioned Audit API. The LuceneSearch keyword was also removed from Audit API conditions in 2025, with "is like" and "is not like" filtering on the Details field in its place, and the Audit Metrics count and size endpoint was retired October 1, 2025.

entries.title: Unversioned Production API (Relativity.Productions.Client)
entries.replacement: Relativity.Productions.SDK, or the versioned REST URLs
entries.customer_wording: The unversioned Production APIs have been deprecated and unsupported in aiR since July 28, 2023. If your code references Relativity.Productions.Client or calls the non-versioned Production URL, switch to Relativity.Productions.SDK or the versioned REST endpoints.

entries.title: Classic List Page API (Relativity.ListPage)
entries.replacement: Relativity Lists API
entries.customer_wording: The classic list page API (Relativity.ListPage) has been replaced by Relativity.Lists in aiR. Third-party apps with List Page Interaction event handlers needed equivalent Relativity.Lists handlers by July 31, 2025, and some events such as listPageChange and newItemButtonInit were removed. The Classic List Page API deprecation page walks through what changed and what to use instead.

entries.title: Analytics Classification API
entries.replacement: none listed
entries.customer_wording: The Analytics Classification API (.NET and REST) was removed from aiR on December 20, 2024, and the changelog doesn't name a direct replacement. Any code that calls it needs to be redesigned before the move.

entries.title: Processing API v0 and v1 document/filter managers
entries.replacement: Processing API v2
entries.customer_wording: aiR has moved the Processing API to v2. The v1 ProcessingDocumentManager and ProcessingFilterManager were removed January 6, 2026 in favor of v2, which uses a string LogicalID instead of the long FileID, the v0 APIs stopped working July 6, 2026, and the static filter endpoints (CreateExpressionFilterAsync, GetFiltersAsync, and the rest) were removed July 14, 2026. Port these calls to Processing API v2.

entries.title: Writing to the Errors tab / Errors API
entries.replacement: Job-level error surfacing, IAPILog
entries.customer_wording: The Errors tab was removed from aiR in July 2025, and as of January 2026 the Errors API is only a stub, so no error data gets written. Code that writes to the Errors tab won't fail, but nobody will ever see those errors. Send them to your app's own logging, or surface them in your job's status instead.

entries.title: Legacy Relativity.ObjectManager NuGet package
entries.replacement: Relativity.ObjectManager.SDK
entries.customer_wording: The legacy Relativity.ObjectManager NuGet package is deprecated. Per the Developer Changelog it was marked deprecated June 22, 2026 and is scheduled to be removed from NuGet in October 2026. Switch the reference to Relativity.ObjectManager.SDK.

entries.title: Legacy Document Viewer Kepler endpoints
entries.replacement: New Document Viewer REST endpoints
entries.customer_wording: The legacy Document Viewer Kepler API endpoints are deprecated in aiR and replaced with new REST API endpoints, per the June 18, 2026 Developer Changelog entry. Code that calls the old Document Viewer services should move to the new REST endpoints, and the developer group post linked from the changelog has the details.

entries.title: Workspace Manager deprecated endpoints and fields
entries.replacement: See developer group posts linked from the changelog
entries.customer_wording: Several Workspace Manager endpoints were deprecated in aiR on August 3, 2026, and the UpdateAsync (PUT) endpoint is deprecated as of December 9, 2026. EnableDataGrid is also deprecated and is always set to true when creating or updating workspaces. The developer group posts linked from the Developer Changelog list the affected endpoints and what replaces them, so check any code that creates or updates workspaces against them.

detection.hint: Workspace creation in aiR is asynchronous, so code that creates a workspace and then configures it right away has to wait for the creation job to finish.

entries.title: Batch Sets Manager and Batches Manager APIs
entries.replacement: TBD (see developer group post)
entries.customer_wording: The Batch Sets Manager and Batches Manager .NET APIs and REST endpoints are scheduled to be deprecated in aiR on March 1, 2027, per the Developer Changelog. If your app creates or reads batch sets through these APIs, plan the change now and check the developer group post linked from the changelog for the recommended path.

entries.title: Keyboard Shortcuts Manager API
entries.replacement: TBD (see developer group post)
entries.customer_wording: The Keyboard Shortcuts Manager .NET API and REST endpoints are scheduled to be deprecated in aiR on February 15, 2027, per the Developer Changelog. If your app manages keyboard shortcuts through this API, plan the change now and check the developer group post linked from the changelog.

entries.title: Cold Storage endpoints and the workspace Status field
entries.replacement: Workspace State field, current Cold Storage API
entries.customer_wording: In aiR, Cold Storage is driven only by the system Workspace State field. Since July 1, 2025 the customer-defined Status field no longer affects Cold Storage or billing, and since September 20, 2026 moving a workspace to Cold Storage doesn't update Status either. CanManageColdStorageAsync and DeleteWorkspaceFromColdStorageAsync were removed July 1, 2026, so scripts and integrations should read Workspace State and use the current Cold Storage API.

entries.title: Relativity Testing Framework (RTF)
entries.replacement: Call the Relativity APIs directly from tests
entries.customer_wording: The Relativity Testing Framework for aiR was removed on May 31, 2024, including the NuGet package and its docs. It's still available for Server, but tests that target aiR should call the Relativity APIs directly. This only affects test projects, not the app you ship.

entries.title: Legacy Import API (WinEDDS / DataExchange based)
entries.replacement: Import Service API (REST) / Relativity.Import.SDK; Export Service API for exports
entries.customer_wording: The legacy Import API (kCura.Relativity.ImportAPI, WinEDDS, DataExchange) doesn't work in aiR. It stopped functioning January 31, 2024, the DataExchange.Client.SDK was deprecated December 2, 2024, and the RDC hasn't worked in aiR since July 1, 2024. Use the Import Service API (REST) or Relativity.Import.SDK for loads, and the Export Service API for exports.

entries.title: Legacy Transfer API (TAPI, Relativity.Transfer.Client) and old Transfer SDK versions
entries.replacement: Relativity.Transfer.SDK (current version)
entries.customer_wording: The old Transfer API (Relativity.Transfer.Client with the Aspera and fileshare clients) doesn't work in aiR, and versions 7.4.10 and below stopped working January 31, 2024. The aiR Relativity.Transfer.SDK is a different API, versions before 4.2.2 stopped working August 3, 2026, and an update to the latest SDK was required on October 15, 2026. Build against the current Relativity.Transfer.SDK.

entries.title: Legacy permissions API writes and SQL writes to permission tables
entries.replacement: Access Control API / Next-Gen permissions API
entries.customer_wording: In aiR, legacy SQL permissions for Staging Reports and Usage Reports were retired on November 10, 2026 as those features moved to the next-gen permission model, and the Permissions API no longer assigns them. Code that sets those permissions should switch to the matching next-gen role keys through the Access Control API.

entries.title: Server-side custom pages (ASP.NET Web Forms and MVC)
entries.replacement: Same page, refactored to the migration checklist; or a static HTML/JS page calling REST APIs
entries.customer_wording: Server-side custom pages, including MVC, still run in aiR, but on Relativity's hosted compute with stricter rules. Pages have to be stateless with no ASP.NET Session State, handle cold caches, ship as one custom page zip per application, and can't use SignalR, ASMX web methods, or admin rights on the host, and most Relativity-hosted assets are gone. Work through the Custom Pages migration checklist, or rebuild simple pages as static HTML and JavaScript that call the REST APIs.

detection.hint: Server-side custom pages still run in aiR. Check the page against the custom page migration checklist (stateless, no session state, single zip, no SignalR).
MVC custom pages still run in aiR. Check the page against the custom page migration checklist.

entries.title: Classic Forms customizations under Relativity Forms
entries.replacement: Relativity Forms API (JavaScript pipelines via ScriptFileNames)
entries.customer_wording: In aiR every object uses Relativity Forms, so classic layout customizations need rework. Script only loads from files listed in the handler's ScriptFileNames, HTML in a handler Message shows as plain text, script in custom text, labels, and HTML fields is sanitized, .NET handlers can't redirect, and PreLoad doesn't fire for new objects (use replaceGetNewObjectInstance in JavaScript). The Migrating to Relativity Forms guide covers each change, including Console event handlers.

entries.title: Relativity Scripts (custom SQL scripts)
entries.replacement: APIs or native features (see sql-to-api-converter skill); Automated Workflows for some
entries.customer_wording: Relativity is retiring the scripts framework in aiR, so SQL-based Relativity Scripts, including ones packaged inside an app, aren't something to carry over. Admins also can't add custom scripts themselves in aiR. Move each script's logic to the Relativity APIs or a native feature as part of the migration.

entries.title: Agents on aiR's compute platform
entries.replacement: Retry plus shutdown pattern from the resiliency guidelines; Relativity.Platform.Agent.WorkloadDiscovery.SDK for scaling
entries.customer_wording: In aiR, Relativity runs and scales your agents, so there are no agent servers to manage. Each agent process gets 1 vCPU and 1 GB of RAM, and to scale out or run on an interval under 60 minutes you add a Workload Discovery endpoint. Agents can occasionally lose connectivity, so HTTP and fileshare calls need retries, and an agent that can't recover should exit so it gets a fresh host. Agents link to your app through Resource Files.

detection.hint_if_lacking: No Workload Discovery endpoint was found in the scanned code, so this agent won't scale dynamically and can't run on an interval under 60 minutes in aiR.

entries.title: Managing agents, servers, and resource pools from code
entries.replacement: none (Relativity manages agents)
entries.customer_wording: Agents, servers, and resource pools are managed by Relativity in aiR. The Agent Manager, Server, and Server Utility APIs aren't documented for aiR, and the Agents, Servers, and Resource Pools tabs are secured by default. If your app creates agents or edits the AgentType table at install time, plan to drop that step and talk to Support about how the agents should be set up.

entries.title: Instance settings changed by apps
entries.replacement: Create app-section settings from a run-once post-install event handler; ask Support for Relativity-owned settings
entries.customer_wording: In aiR, changes to Relativity's own instance settings go through Product Support, and the Instance Settings tab is secured by default. Apps can still create settings in their own section, and the documented pattern is to do that from a run-once post-install event handler using the Instance Setting Manager. Code that edits Relativity-owned settings or writes the InstanceSetting table directly needs to change.

entries.title: Invariant API
entries.replacement: Processing API
entries.customer_wording: The Invariant API is private and isn't available to custom apps in aiR. Code that calls the processing engine directly needs to move to the Processing API.

entries.title: Object Query Manager and View Fields Manager APIs
entries.replacement: Object Manager API (query)
entries.customer_wording: The Object Query Manager and View Fields Manager APIs were deprecated and removed, and they aren't available in aiR. Queries should go through the Object Manager API, and the Object Manager migration guide shows how to convert the code.

docs.title: Migrating code to the Object Manager API

entries.title: Legacy unversioned Imaging and Tab Manager methods
entries.replacement: Versioned Imaging API and Tab Manager API
entries.customer_wording: The unversioned Imaging and Tab Manager methods (for example SaveAsync on the imaging profile and imaging set managers, and GetAvailableObjectTypesAsync, GetAvailableParentsAsync, and GetDependencyList on Tab Manager) were replaced by versioned APIs. Move to the versioned Imaging and Tab Manager APIs, which use separate Create and Update methods and renamed Tab Manager methods.

entries.title: Integration Points kCura.* namespaces
entries.replacement: Relativity.IntegrationPoints.* namespaces and current DLLs
entries.customer_wording: Custom Integration Points providers built on the kCura.IntegrationPoints.* namespaces need to move to Relativity.IntegrationPoints.* and the current DLLs. Also, as of August 29, 2025 the legacy load file import and export workflows in Integration Points are no longer supported in aiR, so use the Import and Export APIs for that work.

entries.title: Removed main-window JavaScript functions and hosted libraries
entries.replacement: Bundle libraries in the page, use window.relativity.* APIs and native browser APIs
entries.customer_wording: Many helper functions on Relativity's main window (RelativityAjax, PopWindow, GetApplicationPath, confirmYesNo, and others) and the libraries Relativity used to host (AngularJS, jQuery, jQuery UI, Knockout, and so on) aren't available to custom pages in aiR. Bundle any libraries your page needs, use window.relativity.* for values like getApplicationPath and getKeplerApplicationPath, and switch to native browser APIs like fetch. The Removals page lists every item with its replacement.

entries.title: Shipping assemblies that clash with platform-provided ones
entries.replacement: Use the platform-provided version, or internalize the dependency
entries.customer_wording: aiR supplies a number of assemblies itself, and an app that ships its own copy of one can break, sometimes only after a platform update. For example, the agent framework supports Polly 5.7.0 only and the docs say not to add it to your app, and the External Logging docs warn that dependencies that conflict with the platform's will break the app. Use the platform-provided version, or internalize the dependency so it can't clash.

entries.title: Pre-2022 unversioned Kepler API namespaces and URLs
entries.replacement: The versioned (V1+) namespace and REST URL for each API
entries.customer_wording: Apps built for Server 10.3 or 2021 that use the old unversioned Kepler namespaces and URLs need to move to the versioned contracts, for example Relativity.Environment.V1.Workspace and the relativity-environment/v1 REST paths. Relativity moved to versioned namespaces API by API starting with Server 2022, and aiR uses the versioned forms.

entries.title: Object Manager request rate limits and data egress limits
entries.replacement: Pace with RateLimit headers, retry on Retry-After, send X-Kepler-Referrer, use Export Service API for bulk text
entries.customer_wording: Object Manager in aiR limits each application to 1,000 requests per minute per web server and returns 429 Too Many Requests above that, per the Developer Changelog. The StreamLongText endpoint is also rate limited as of September 1, 2026. Pace your calls, retry after a 429, and use the Export Service API for bulk text instead of streaming long text one field at a time.

detection.hint: Object Manager calls were found but nothing in the scanned code sets the X-Kepler-Referrer header. Object Manager identifies each consumer by that header when it applies its rate limit.
Object Manager calls were found but nothing in the scanned code sets the X-Kepler-Referrer header. Object Manager identifies each consumer by that header when it applies its rate limit.

entries.title: Audit and login data read straight from SQL
entries.replacement: Audit API (relativity-audit/v1)
entries.customer_wording: Use the Audit API for audit and login data in aiR. The login history library scripts (Login History by User Report and Environment-Level User Login) are retired, and Relativity points to Audit for similar data.

entries.title: ARM API V1, Relativity.ARM.SDK, and unversioned ARM URLs
entries.replacement: ARM REST API V3
entries.customer_wording: ARM REST API V3 is the version to build against in aiR, and Relativity publishes a V1 to V3 migration guide. Integrations still calling ARM V1 or unversioned ARM URLs should follow that guide and move to V3.

plan_for.title: Installing complex custom applications
plan_for.customer_wording: In aiR the Application Library tab is hidden, and Relativity prefers that complex custom apps get installed through Product Support so it can check infrastructure, scale agents, and confirm compatibility. Plan the install with Support as part of the migration rather than uploading the RAP yourself.

plan_for.title: Classic Viewer extensions
plan_for.customer_wording: The Classic Viewer was deprecated in October 2021 and removed from Server 2023, so it isn't available in aiR. Viewer extensions built for it need to be rebuilt as Review Interface extensions using the Review API.
